mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and thus leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which is typically associated with robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 2% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which is typically associated with positive economic sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) also decline over the same period, it indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS declines YoY
failure_condition: If HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS declines YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of economic expansion, a significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust economic growth, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.
